matchups.recap:
Week 3 pitted The Machine Knows against Rome-ans 10:9-10 in what amounted to a Bust Hike for the Lone Eagle, who scraped out a 97.04-92.16 win despite Omarion Hampton and Justin Jefferson both walking on the alpine vegetation. Jefferson's 4.2 points against a near-15 projection is the kind of afternoon that gets a camper quietly reassigned to dish duty, but Lamar Jackson's 20.44 and Jaylen Warren carrying the load like a Woodsman Chief on a hike papered over the mess. Call it a well-earned Tuna Casserole earned more by Golden's cabin failing to show up than by any real mastery of the course.

The Machine Knows, meanwhile, got its lunch eaten by Yellow Yellow at the receiver position, where Malik Nabers turned a 12-point projection into a Dutch Oven-adjacent 5.1. Matthew Golden, Javonte Williams, and Josh Allen all put in Boss shifts, but three good hikers can't carry a cabin when the fourth is stuck bushwhacking without a compass. Preseason Power Rankings #1 or not, this counselor needs a better plan before the leaderboard starts believing its own preseason hype.

matchups.winner: Chase Brown Had a Bad Scare
matchups.recap:
This week's woods course belonged entirely to Pill Pusher, who sent Brock Purdy out for 31.28 and let Drake London and Christian McCaffrey mop up the rest, cruising to 126.58 with the kind of feel for the week that makes a camp director's job easy. It was less a matchup than a Bust Hike that never actually got hard — 35.14 points of cushion means nobody was sweating the compass on this one. Sticky buns on Sunday morning, well-earned Tuna Casserole, the works.

Chef Boyardee, real name Stefanowitcz for those keeping score at home, ran his Goose cabin straight into the alpine vegetation. Jonathan Taylor turned a 19.1 projection into 8.2, TreVeyon Henderson ate his trail cheese and salami for 3.4, and Tetairoa McMillan's 2.7 points made him look like a stunned naval battle queen out there. Brock Bowers and Dak Prescott tried to carry the canoe alone but the rest of the roster chose the Canoe Hike, and by the fourth quarter the whole operation looked like a Woodsman playing Chief Tyler Hallenbeck in Tetherball. Bushwhacking without a compass, and no amount of Goose honking fixes that.

Catalina Wine Mixon, the Chair Force this week, got the trip up to 104.24 despite De'Von Achane basically staying in the cabin with a 1.7, and Rhamondre Stevenson doing his part to make sure nobody trusted the canoe. Jeremiyah Love and the Vikings D/ST did the carrying, Mahomes chipped in without needing to be great, and the whole operation walked away with sticky buns on Sunday morning even with two backs bushwhacking without a compass all afternoon.

Love Thy Naber is stuck on the Point and Back after dropping to 1-2, and Dalton Kincaid deserves a long look in the mirror after his 2.8 stole my wow while Juwan Johnson lit up the box score from the bench. Stafford and James Cook III kept the canoe upright, but Jadarian Price's 0.7 dragged the whole plan into the alpine vegetation. The counselor's read on this week was off from the start, and now it is two straight losses with nobody around camp letting them forget it.

Camp store shift this week went to The Island Gudge, who ran a clinic while Harley Jarvis wandered the woods without a map. Joe Burrow's 22.58, Garrett Wilson's 21.7, and Kenneth Walker III's 20.3 all carried the load like a Woodsman Chief on a hike, and the 46er had all the arrows in the bullseye from the opening whistle. A 41-point margin isn't a Bust Hike, it's a post hike scrub, and everyone in that cabin is earning sticky buns on Sunday morning tonight.

Harley Jarvis, meanwhile, chose the Canoe Hike and never recovered. Isaiah Likely's 2.3 and an Eagles D/ST that finished at -1.0 point to a counselor bushwhacking without a compass on defense, and the whole operation is stuck on the Point and Back after back-to-back losses. Ja'Marr Chase's 20.3 was Boss enough on its own, but with the Eagles D/ST actively subtracting points, the rest of the cabin had its lunch eaten by Yellow Yellow. Regroup at the flagpole, gentlemen — the compass is right there on the shelf.

Ricky Huns turned Camp Activities Night into a full-on wipeout, running the largest margin of victory anywhere on the lake this week and never once looking back. Other Nate had George Kittle out there carrying the load like a Woodsman Chief on a hike with 23.2, got a bonus haul from Michael Wilson's 20.4, and Kyren Williams chipped in 18.8 for good measure. The plan was crisp, the bench barely mattered, and by the time the final whistle blew this one was a straight post hike scrub. Somewhere across the lake a counselor is standing on a picnic table yelling I want you to BRING DOWN THE ROOF, and this week he's earned it.

Funk that Junk, meanwhile, went bushwhacking without a compass from the opening horn. Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 30.36 and Deebo Samuel's 15.4 were about the only things keeping this from total humiliation, because Breece Hall and Bucky Irving both ate their trail cheese and salami on the ground, and Drake Maye put up a stunned naval battle queen 3.76 that had Sir Jo-Nurse burying his head in a canoe. A gonna-need-more-leaves kind of week all around — soaking wet, Beak from top to bottom.

Paralegal sent 55 Burgers out on the trail with Mark Andrews and KC Concepcion supposedly ready to work, and both showed up empty-handed, 3.9 and 1.9 points of pure bushwhacking without a compass. Jahmyr Gibbs ran like a woodsman running to the camp store all day long, but one man carrying the packs while the rest of the cabin ate its lunch courtesy of Yellow Yellow is how you end up stuck in the Sewards. This cabin is stuck on the Point and Back after dropping a second straight, and Concepcion in particular was living like living on the Point at a spot on the roster that badly needed more.

Team Bradford, the Campcraft Enthusiast's crew, ran a pig and back all week and it showed — Bijan Robinson carried the load like a Woodsman Chief on a hike with 34.3, Derrick Henry chipped in 21.4, and Harold Fannin Jr. added another 20.6 for good measure. Jalen Coker was the lone soaking-wet leaf patch at 2.8, but with that much firepower elsewhere it barely mattered. A comfortable, well-earned Tuna Casserole night — Team Bradford earned a post hike scrub and left 55 Burgers wondering what happened to their compass.

headline: Week 3 delivers blowouts, one nail biter, six new records
